intent: Fix Vercel ISR requests that returned 404 by restoring the original route from the x_astro_path query parameter before Astro route matching. The change should preserve the route and query behavior expected by the application.

findings.title: ISR exposes its internal path query parameter to pages
findings.suggested_fix: After reading x_astro_path for the route rewrite, remove that adapter-only parameter from the URL search parameters before constructing the Request passed to Astro, while retaining other query parameters.
findings.why_it_matters: ISR pages receive the adapter's internal x_astro_path parameter as part of their request URL. Page code that reads Astro.url.searchParams or builds a canonical URL from the request sees a parameter that was added only to route the request through Vercel's ISR function, changing application-visible query behavior.
evidence: packages/integrations/vercel/src/serverless/entrypoint.ts:29-34 -- The request is reconstructed from url.toString() and then passed to app.match() and app.render().
packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:63 -- The ISR destination adds x_astro_path to the query string.
packages/integrations/vercel/src/index.ts:712 -- The ISR config sets passQuery: true, so the handler receives the rewritten query parameter.

residual_risks: The adversarial reviewer noted a possible interaction if edge middleware intercepts rewritten `/_isr` requests and supplies its internal URL through the secret-protected path header; the supplied evidence does not establish that sequence.
testing_gaps: The ISR tests verify generated routes and prerender configuration, but do not invoke the built ISR handler with x-vercel-isr: 1 and assert that the original route is restored. A handler-level regression could let ISR requests return 404 again while the existing route-generation assertions still pass.
